questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 6]

For six teenagers, talking time T (min):50,55,105,128,155,200 and messages M:358,340,740,731,800,992. Model M=aT+b. (a) Write a,b. [3] (b) Predict M at T=154. [3]
questions.summary: For six teenagers, talking time T (min):50,55,105,128,155,200 and messages M:358,340,740,731,800,992. Model M=aT+b. (a) Write a,b. [3] (b) Predict M at T=154. [3]
questions.solution: Regression gives a=4.3016108…, b=163.3306…, hence a=4.30,b=163. At T=154, M=825.779…, so predict 826 messages. This agrees with the official markscheme.

2. [Maximum mark: 5]

Lines L₁:y=−(2/3)x+9 and L₂:y=(2/5)x−19/5. (a) Find intersection. [2] L₃ has gradient −3/4. (b) Give a direction vector. [1] (c) L₃ passes through the intersection; give vector equation. [2]
questions.summary: Lines L₁:y=−(2/3)x+9 and L₂:y=(2/5)x−19/5. (a) Find intersection. [2] L₃ has gradient −3/4. (b) Give a direction vector. [1] (c) L₃ passes through the intersection; give vector equ
questions.solution: (a) Equating gives x=12,y=1. (b) A direction vector is (4,−3). (c) r=(12,1)+t(4,−3), t∈ℝ. This agrees with the official markscheme.

questions.accessible_text:
3. [Maximum mark: 7]

Let f(x)=x−8, g(x)=x⁴−3 and h(x)=f(g(x)). (a) Find h. [2] At C on h, its tangent is parallel to graph f. (b) Find x-coordinate of C. [5]
questions.summary: Let f(x)=x−8, g(x)=x⁴−3 and h(x)=f(g(x)). (a) Find h. [2] At C on h, its tangent is parallel to graph f. (b) Find x-coordinate of C. [5]
questions.solution: (a) h(x)=x⁴−11. (b) Graph f has slope 1. Since h′=4x³, set 4x³=1, giving x=∛(1/4)=0.630. This agrees with the official markscheme.

questions.accessible_text:
4. [Maximum mark: 7]

Right triangle ABC has AC=10 cm, AB=6 cm, BC=8 cm. D,F lie on AC; BD⊥AC; arc BEF is centred at A. Region R is bounded by BD,DF and arc BEF. [Diagram not to scale.] (a) Find angle BAC. [2] (b) Find area R. [5]
questions.summary: Right triangle ABC has AC=10 cm, AB=6 cm, BC=8 cm. D,F lie on AC; BD⊥AC; arc BEF is centred at A. Region R is bounded by BD,DF and arc BEF. [Diagram not to scale.] (a) Find angle B
questions.solution: (a) cosA=AB/AC=0.6, so A=0.927295… rad=53.1°. (b) Radius AB=AF=6. Sector ABF area=(1/2)6²A=16.6913. Similar/right-triangle geometry gives AD=AB²/AC=3.6 and BD=4.8, so triangle ABD area=8.64. Thus R=16.6913−8.64=8.05 cm². This agrees with the official markscheme.

questions.accessible_text:
5. [Maximum mark: 7]

Geometric sequence u₁=2.1,u₂=2.226. (a) Find r. [2] (b) Find u₁₀. [2] (c) Find least n with Sₙ>5543. [3]
questions.summary: Geometric sequence u₁=2.1,u₂=2.226. (a) Find r. [2] (b) Find u₁₀. [2] (c) Find least n with Sₙ>5543. [3]
questions.solution: (a) r=2.226/2.1=1.06. (b) u₁₀=2.1(1.06)^9=3.55. (c) Solve 2.1(1.06^n−1)/0.06>5543; n=87 is insufficient and n=88 works, so n=88. This agrees with the official markscheme.

questions.accessible_text:
6. [Maximum mark: 6]

A triangular-based pyramid has base ADC; BD⊥AD and BD⊥CD. [Diagram: AC=28.4 cm, AB=x, BC=x+2, angle ABC=0.667 rad, angle BAD=0.611 rad.] Calculate AD.
questions.summary: A triangular-based pyramid has base ADC; BD⊥AD and BD⊥CD. [Diagram: AC=28.4 cm, AB=x, BC=x+2, angle ABC=0.667 rad, angle BAD=0.611 rad.] Calculate AD.
questions.solution: Cosine rule in ABC: 28.4²=x²+(x+2)²−2x(x+2)cos0.667. The positive solution is x=42.2822…. In right triangle ABD, AD=ABcos0.611=42.2822cos0.611=34.6 cm. This agrees with the official markscheme.

questions.accessible_text:
7. [Maximum mark: 7]

Discrete X has values 1,4,a,a+b−0.5 with probabilities 0.2,0.5,b,a, where a,b≥0. (a) Show b=0.3−a. [1] (b) Find difference between greatest and least possible E(X). [6]
questions.summary: Discrete X has values 1,4,a,a+b−0.5 with probabilities 0.2,0.5,b,a, where a,b≥0. (a) Show b=0.3−a. [1] (b) Find difference between greatest and least possible E(X). [6]
questions.solution: (a) Probabilities sum: .2+.5+a+b=1, so b=.3−a and 0≤a≤.3. (b) Substitution gives E=0.2+2+a(.3−a)+(−.2)a=2.2+0.1a−a². Maximum at a=.05 is 2.2025; minimum on [0,.3] is E(.3)=2.14. Difference=0.0625. This agrees with the official markscheme.

questions.accessible_text:
8. [Maximum mark: 16]

f(x)=x⁴−54x²+60x, −1≤x≤6. [Graph: intercepts 0,p; maximum A at x=a; inflexion B at x=b.] (a) Find p. [2] (b)(i) coordinates A; (ii) tangent at A. [4] (c)(i) coordinates B; (ii) rate of change at B. [7] (d) Region between graph,x-axis,x=p,x=b is rotated about x-axis; find volume. [3]
questions.summary: f(x)=x⁴−54x²+60x, −1≤x≤6. [Graph: intercepts 0,p; maximum A at x=a; inflexion B at x=b.] (a) Find p. [2] (b)(i) coordinates A; (ii) tangent at A. [4] (c)(i) coordinates B; (ii) rat
questions.solution: (a) On −1≤x≤6, the non-zero intercept is p=1.138434…≈1.14. (b) f′=4x³−108x+60; the local maximum is A=(0.562135…,16.7642…), and its tangent is y=16.7642…. (c) f″=12x²−108, so b=3 and B=(3,−225); f′(3)=−156. (d) V=π∫₁.138434^3[f(x)]²dx=80902.4…≈80900 cm³. This agrees with the official markscheme.

9. [Maximum mark: 15]

Flight time ~N(260,15²); late means >275. (a) P(not late). [2] On time means m to275 with probability .830. (b) Find m. [3] In 12 independent flights: (c)(i) P(at least7 on time); (ii) given at least7, P(exactly10). [7] For 20 improved flights P(at least19)=.788. (d) Find probability one flight is on time. [3]
questions.summary: Flight time ~N(260,15²); late means >275. (a) P(not late). [2] On time means m to275 with probability .830. (b) Find m. [3] In 12 independent flights: (c)(i) P(at least7 on time);
questions.solution: (a) Φ(1)=0.841. (b) Φ((m−260)/15)=Φ(1)−.830=.0113447, so m=225.821≈226 min. (c) With p=.830, binomial calculation gives P(X≥7)=0.991248≈0.991 and P(X=10|X≥7)=0.298566≈0.299. (d) Solve p²⁰+20p¹⁹(1−p)=.788, giving p=0.956962≈0.957. This agrees with the official markscheme.

10. [Maximum mark: 14]

A rocket starts at 140 m/s and reaches 500 m/s in two stages. First-stage acceleration a(t)=240sin(2t), 0≤t≤k. (a) Find velocity. [4] Stage 1 ends at 375 m/s. (b) Find first-stage distance. [4] Stage 2 has constant acceleration and same distance as stage 1. (c) Find total time. [6]
questions.summary: A rocket starts at 140 m/s and reaches 500 m/s in two stages. First-stage acceleration a(t)=240sin(2t), 0≤t≤k. (a) Find velocity. [4] Stage 1 ends at 375 m/s. (b) Find first-stage
questions.solution: (a) v=∫240sin2t dt=−120cos2t+C; v(0)=140 gives v=260−120cos2t. (b) 375=260−120cos2k gives k=(1/2)arccos(−23/24)=1.42595 s. Distance D=∫₀^k vdt=260k−60sin2k=353.609 m. (c) Under constant acceleration from 375 to500, average velocity=437.5, so stage-2 time=D/437.5=0.808248 s. Total=2.23420≈2.23 s. This agrees with the official markscheme.
